title: Subtype Prevalence
description: HIV-1A6 is a notable subtype, being the sixth most common. In Sweden, a significant portion of HIV patients are homosexual males, with 81% of the cases. The country sees approximately 400-500 new HIV cases annually, with men accounting for 64% of these new diagnoses.

title: Demographic Patterns
description: In 2019, the median age of individuals diagnosed with HIV in Sweden was 38 years. Migrants, who constituted 12% of the EU population, represented 44% of new HIV cases. In Sweden, 36% of those living with HIV were born in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting significant demographic patterns in the distribution of HIV cases.

title: Migrant Impact
description: In Sweden, a significant portion of the HIV-positive population consists of migrants, with 80% of those diagnosed being from this group. The country has an estimated 8,000 people living with HIV, with 10% remaining undiagnosed. Among those diagnosed, 78% achieve virological suppression, indicating effective management of the condition.

title: Healthcare Access
description: Sweden has a robust system for managing HIV, with a high percentage of patients receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) and being linked to care. The majority of people living with HIV in Sweden are on ART, and nearly all diagnosed patients are connected to healthcare services. However, migrants, who constitute a significant portion of the population, account for a large percentage of new HIV cases annually.

title: Treatment Success
description: In Sweden, significant progress has been made in managing HIV, with 99% of diagnosed individuals on antiretroviral therapy (ART) by 2022. A high percentage of patients on treatment for at least six months have achieved viral suppression, with 94.7% having a viral load of less than 50 HIV-1 RNA copies/mL. Additionally, 90% of all individuals infected with HIV in Sweden are diagnosed, indicating effective healthcare strategies. The majority of people living with HIV in Sweden are foreign-born, with 64% born abroad, highlighting the diverse demographic affected by the disease.

Additionally, 78% of HIV-infected individuals in Sweden have a suppressed viral load, indicating effective management of the condition.

title: Data Coverage
description: In Sweden, approximately 400-500 new HIV cases are reported annually. By the end of 2015, 95% of individuals on antiretroviral treatment had a viral load below 50 copies/ml. The prevalence of HIV in Sweden is estimated at 0.07% of the population. InfCareHIV tracks over 99% of diagnosed cases, ensuring comprehensive data coverage. By 2022, 96% of people with HIV were diagnosed, and diagnoses of endogenous acquisitions reached 96%.
